title: The Secret of the Celebrity Couple
notes: Recurring detective-cast (Conan, Inspector Megure, Detective Chiba, Kogoro) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old cases/ep856 file's culprit call (s2 = Maiko Hori) checks out against the transcript -- Hori Maiko really is the one who killed Saki -- but two of its details were off and are corrected here: (1) its clue c1 says the staircase camera was broken 'two weeks' in advance; the transcript states 'two days ago' (line ~113). (2) its event e2 vaguely says Hori 'suffocates Saki herself and stages the scene to look like a robbery gone wrong'; the transcript's actual reveal is more specific -- Saki staged HER OWN death scene to look like she was a robbery victim who accidentally suffocated (self-bound arms/legs, tape over her own mouth) as cover for having murdered her husband Seiichi; Hori was summoned as accomplice to help dispose of the murder weapon, but instead pressed the tape onto Saki's mouth herself and let/made her suffocate for real, then camouflaged the closet to look like an accident. The forensic tell is the contrast between the bands (only Saki's prints -- self-applied) and the tape (Hori's prints plus multiple struggle-smudges of lipstick -- someone else applied it). Old file also had no node for the husband-victim Seiichi as a person (folded into event prose); given a full person node here since he is the first murder victim. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Only Saki's fingerprints were on the binding bands (self-applied), but Maiko Hori's prints turned up on the tape over Saki's mouth -- the tape was applied by someone else.
The tape carried several lipstick smudges from a struggle, not the single clean mark self-application would leave -- someone else pressed it onto Saki's face.

The weapon sat in the dumpster for two full days before collection -- too careless a hiding spot if Saki alone staged and executed the whole scheme; implies an accomplice was meant to move it but never got the chance.

The closet held more clothes than its volume allows, many previously worn, wrinkled, and smelling of cigarettes rather than freshly hung -- staged after the fact to fake an accident, not consistent with Saki's own careful plan.
